newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty slips back below 1.5 pct resistance.
newsitem.headline: Zloty slips back below 1.5 pct resistance.

text.p: The Polish zloty returned to its weeks-old trading level just under resistance at 1.5 percent from parity on Thursday after briefly venturing higher earlier in the week, dealers said.
Dealers said trading volume was heavy but that the zloty remained range-bound and followed dollar/mark moves on Thursday after some banks rebuild currency positions in early trade .
"Trading was active but the zloty barely moved against the basket...and it should remained anchored around 1.5 percent on Friday," said Tomasz Nowakowski, dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 1.51/1.47 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Wednesday's 1.58/1.53 percent close.
It closed at 3.2450/70 to the dollar, down from 3.2367/77 on Wednesday and at 1.8727/32 to the mark, up from 1.8741/54.

Overnight rates ended lower at 21.00/21.30 percent vs opening's 21.60/21.70 and tomorrow/next at 21.30/21.60 from 21.60/21.75 despite Thursday's 1.93 billion zloty central bank drainage as the market remained slightly overliquid.
The central bank said that Poland's net currency reserves rose to $641 million in May to $21.713 billion.
